title: AgentForge: An Immersive Role-Playing Platform for Learning Agentic Software Engineering
title_zh: AgentForge：用于学习智能体式软件工程的沉浸式角色扮演平台
abstract_en: Agentic AI is increasingly used to coordinate planning, implementation, review, and testing in software development, yet it often offers limited transparency into its decisions and interactions. Many such systems also assume that users can effectively guide the AI's decisions and validate its outputs. This assumption poses a particular challenge for novices, who must simultaneously learn how agentic AI works, how to collaborate with it effectively, and how to evaluate its outputs critically. To address this challenge, we present \textit{AgentForge}, an immersive learning system in which novices take on one of four software-engineering roles: Task Planner, Patch Author, Code Reviewer, or Test Runner, within a multi-agent code-repair workflow. In each practice session, the novices perform their chosen role while AI agents perform the remaining three. Through role-based scaffolding and metacognitive support, AgentForge clarifies role-specific responsibilities, makes agent coordination and intermediate artifacts visible, and encourages novices to monitor and evaluate their decisions. In a study with 37 novice developers, participants achieved high task-completion rates with AI-agent support. However, interaction demands differed significantly across practices: the Code Reviewer practice required more interaction turns, reroutes, and completion time ($p_{\mathrm{adj}} = .004$) and was perceived as the most challenging. Participants nevertheless reported significant gains in their understanding of software repair and agent collaboration ($p_{\mathrm{adj}} < .001$). These findings suggest that AgentForge can help novices develop practical software-engineering skills while learning to collaborate with agentic AI more critically and effectively.
abstract_zh: 随着 Agentic AI 越来越多地用于软件开发中的规划、实现、评审与测试，其决策过程和智能体间交互往往缺乏透明度，并且默认用户具备有效引导 AI 决策、验证 AI 输出的能力。对于新手开发者而言，这意味着他们需要同时学习 Agentic AI 的工作机制、如何与其协作，以及如何批判性评估其结果。为此，论文提出 AgentForge，一个沉浸式学习系统，让新手在多智能体代码修复流程中扮演四类软件工程角色之一：Task Planner、Patch Author、Code Reviewer 或 Test Runner，其余三个角色由 AI agents 执行。AgentForge 通过基于角色的脚手架与元认知支持，明确各角色职责，展示智能体协作过程与中间产物，并鼓励学习者监控和评估自身决策。在包含 37 名新手开发者的研究中，参与者在 AI-agent 支持下实现了较高任务完成率；但不同实践的交互负担显著不同，其中 Code Reviewer 需要更多交互轮次、重路由和完成时间（调整后 p = .004），也被认为最具挑战性。尽管如此，参与者在软件修复与智能体协作理解方面均报告了显著提升（调整后 p < .001）。结果表明，AgentForge 有助于新手在发展软件工程实践能力的同时，更批判、有效地学习与 Agentic AI 协作。
key_points_zh: 提出 AgentForge，一个面向新手的软件工程学习平台，通过沉浸式角色扮演帮助用户理解多智能体代码修复流程。
系统设计四个角色：Task Planner、Patch Author、Code Reviewer 和 Test Runner；学习者扮演其中一个，其余由 AI agents 完成。
AgentForge 强调角色脚手架、元认知支持和过程可视化，使智能体协作、中间产物与决策责任更加透明。
37 名新手开发者研究显示，AI-agent 支持下任务完成率较高，但 Code Reviewer 任务交互成本最高、主观难度最大。
参与者在软件修复理解与 Agentic AI 协作认知上显著提升，说明该平台可用于培养更批判有效的人机协作能力。

llm_assessment.comment: Mostly an educational human-learning platform around agentic software workflows rather than reusable agent harness or evaluation infrastructure.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: 这主要是围绕智能体软件流程的教育学习平台，而不是可复用的智能体运行或评测基础设施。
